title: The modified integer round-up conjecture for cutting stock
decision_reason: Exact all-pattern formulation, independently authored corroboration, twelve scope comparisons, duplicate review, separated A54 self-review and technical validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.input: For every n>=1, positive integer stock capacity W, positive integer item lengths ell_i<=W, and positive integer demands b_i, i=1,...,n.
problem_fingerprint.pattern_set: All nonnegative integer vectors a with sum_i ell_i a_i<=W. No demand-dependent cap a_i<=b_i is imposed; nonproper patterns are allowed.
problem_fingerprint.integer_optimum: z_IP=min sum_a x_a subject to sum_a a_i x_a>=b_i for every i and x_a nonnegative integers.
problem_fingerprint.fractional_optimum: z_LP is the same finite pattern formulation with x_a nonnegative real numbers.
problem_fingerprint.question: Does z_IP<=ceil(z_LP)+1 hold for every such instance?
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Arbitrary number of item types, arbitrary capacity, lengths and demands; the additive one is uniform across all instances.
problem_fingerprint.objective: Total number of stock pieces, counting repeated patterns separately; not the number of distinct patterns or trim loss.
problem_fingerprint.canonical_scope: One offline cutting-stock/bin-packing LP-gap family. Proper-pattern restrictions, special item classes and weaker constant-gap questions are not counted separately.
problem_fingerprint.computational_scope: A structural relation between optima; no polynomial-time construction or algorithmic rounding guarantee is required.

§1 equation (1), pp. 1–2, general pattern LP and MIRUP discussion.

independently_authored_corroboration.independence: The three author teams are disjoint from one another and from the original Scheithauer–Terno authors.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: The exact ceiling-plus-one question is retained in the June 2026 primary preprint; the 2015 algorithmic paper and 2020 counterexample survey supply independent formulation/status context.

nearest_existing.comparison: Unknown adversarial arrivals and irrevocable placements; asks for a deterministic asymptotic multiplicative competitive ratio. The present offline assertion compares integer and fractional optima additively.
Uniform infinity-norm discrepancy for signed prefixes of Euclidean unit vectors. Discrepancy can inform rounding methods, but it is not this fixed knapsack-pattern optimum inequality.
A multiplicative Held–Karp gap for metric tours; different feasible configurations, polytope and objective.

issues_found: Proper and nonproper pattern relaxations can be conflated; their integer optima coincide but their fractional optima need not.
Counterexamples to ordinary IRUP and a distinct-pattern conjecture may look like MIRUP refutations.
Recent benchmark algorithms, high-multiplicity runtime bounds and multiflow integrality results concern different guarantees.
A proof title refers to at most seven item sizes; divisible-instance bounds retain an extra hypothesis.
One recent overflow paper has a replacement notice, and one old arXiv PDF has a typesetting date different from its submission history.
A logarithmic asymptotic bound should use a harmless positive-argument convention when displayed for all positive LP values.
issues_resolved: Retained all capacity-feasible patterns, arbitrary demands, covering constraints and exact ceiling-plus-one target; documented downward-closure normalization.
Read complete G20 counterexample formulations, EPR12 algorithm-class definition and KKRS14 pattern definitions/results.
Compared full SLSCI26 theorem hypotheses, JOP26 Theorem 3, ASW26 Theorems 1–2 and the corrected MS26 model.
Checked the complete EPR12 seven-size restatement and M22 Definition 3/Theorem 4; disclosed unavailable original personal communication.
Used the presently served corrected overflow model, recorded the notice's limited detail, and verified the sole KKRS14 arXiv version.
Wrote the logarithmic partial bound as O(log(2+z_LP)), preserving its asymptotic meaning without a nonpositive logarithm for small LP optima.
second_review.quantifier_checks: All n>=1 and all positive integer capacities, lengths <=W and demands; one uniform additive one; same complete pattern set for integer and real variables; no algorithmic, fixed-type, divisibility or proper-pattern promise.
second_review.application_check: Idealized one-dimensional production planning with uniform stock length and stock-count objective; no unsupported guarantee for trim-loss, setup-cost or machine-restricted variants.
second_review.duplicate_check: Fresh aliases searched across active pages, data, manifest and research records; full nearest entries 326, 336 and 285 compared. No equivalent accepted assertion located.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: All ordinary bin-packing instances admit a solution within a logarithmic additive term of the all-pattern LP; randomized expected time is polynomial in total multiplicity.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: A growing logarithmic term does not prove the ceiling-plus-one target. Runtime polynomial in expanded item count does not imply polynomial time in binary multiplicity encoding.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial exact packing for AI instances constructed from a fixed original instance by constrained augmentation.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The reconstruction guarantee requires membership in the constructed class. Running the same procedure on arbitrary instances may return Fail.

resolution_comparisons.locator: §5.1 complete Theorems 2–3, Lemma 1 and algorithm discussion
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Pseudopolynomial exact solution for ANI benchmark classes, using original irreducibility and constrained full triplets; constant-size residual guaranteed for the specified class.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The universal runtime/preprocessing statement does not supply universal optimality or a universal all-pattern LP-gap bound.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Ordinary IRUP counterexample W=132, lengths (44,33,12), demands (2,3,6), LP=259/132, integer optimum=3.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: ceil(259/132)+1=3. It disproves the stronger ordinary rounding assertion while satisfying the displayed MIRUP target.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Nine orders may need eleven distinct patterns in a waste-optimal exact-demand solution.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Support size and waste are different objectives from total stock multiplicity. This is not a counterexample to the number-of-stock-pieces LP-gap conjecture.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Logarithmic and squared-logarithmic barriers for algorithms using the supplied fractional support, with specific domination/discarding rules.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The unrestricted integer optimum can use other feasible patterns. A lower bound for this algorithm class is not an instance with an unrestricted MIRUP violation.

resolution_comparisons.locator: §1, p. 2, explicit Sebő–Shmonin scope restatement and reference [23]
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: The cited partial proof has at most seven distinct item sizes.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The proposed n is unbounded. Only the complete scholarly scope restatement was inspected; the personal communication was not represented as a checked original proof.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: ETH rules out time |I|^(2^o(d)) for exact high-multiplicity bin packing with d sizes and binary input.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Exact optimization complexity does not decide the structural additive gap of the LP. MIRUP neither requires an efficient algorithm nor promises exact optimization from the LP alone.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Integer multiflow rounding and unsplittable flow with per-arc deviation below the maximum commodity demand on series-parallel digraphs.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Integer multiflow need not keep an item whole. Unsplittable rounding permits capacity overflow; the target instead keeps every stock capacity W and bounds the number of pieces.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Enumerates proper-pattern IRUP for small total item counts and constructs proper gaps exceeding one, up to 17/16 in the table.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Ordinary proper IRUP is stronger than proper MIRUP and differs from the all-pattern relaxation. A proper gap below two alone would not bound the all-pattern gap; the paper itself retains the general MIRUP conjecture and makes no general refutation claim.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: The all-pattern cutting-stock gap is <4/3 when W/ell_i is an integer for every i.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Divisibility is an additional hypothesis. The subsequent transfer sentence concerns a skiving-stock bound and is not a universal cutting-stock MIRUP proof.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Fixed-bin overflow optimization minimizes total absolute deviations; one equal-size item/bin pair can be fixed in an optimum.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Capacity overflow, fixed bin count and a deviation objective change the model. Neither the corrected result nor MS26C announces a classical cutting-stock MIRUP theorem.

normalization_checks.proper_patterns: Restricting a_i<=b_i can increase the LP optimum; it must not silently replace the all-pattern relaxation. The draft uses the explicit SLSCI26 Property 2 convention.
normalization_checks.covering_vs_equality: For the complete downward-closed pattern set, surplus production can be removed without adding stock pieces. In the LP, a fractional amount of a pattern a can be replaced by a-e_i until surplus in coordinate i is removed, preserving cost and other coordinates. Thus exact-demand statements with this full pattern set also apply to the displayed covering optima. This elementary normalization is not a proof of MIRUP.
normalization_checks.ceiling: For integral z_IP, z_IP<=ceil(z_LP)+1 is equivalent to z_IP-z_LP<2, including integral z_LP. It is not the stronger inequality z_IP-z_LP<=1.
normalization_checks.small_lp: The source's O(log OPT_f) asymptotic bound is written O(log(2+z_LP)) to cover small positive LP values. If z_LP<=1 then total item length<=W and all demanded items fit in one stock piece.
